To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the in vitro activation of tonsil and skin human mast cells with PAR-2 agonist peptides and trypsin, which is a physiological agonist of PAR-2, suggested a novel mast cell heterogeneity and a self-amplifying mechanism of mast cell activation.

PAR‐2 agonist peptide, SLIGKV, induced degranulation of mast cells, and trypsin induced a “bell”‐shape increase in tryptaste release from tonsil and histamine release from both tonsil mast cells and skin mast cells.
PAR-2 is a novel mast cell activation receptor, which can induce degranulation in a self-amplifying manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the activation of human mast cells by PAR agonists, trypsin and histamine.
the activation of mast cells in response to PAR-2 agonist peptides.
the role of PAR-2 in mast cell biology.

the activation of mast cell degradulation was dependent upon the activation of PAR-2 and the release of histamine was a result of the activation of PAR‐2 and histamine release.
human mast cells are capable of degranulating in response to PAR-2 agonist peptides, and this activation is independent of histamine release.
PAR-2 is a novel mast cell receptor and may have important roles in allergic diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mast cell activation by trypsin is mediated via PAR-2, and the activation of PAR-2 by PAR-2 ligands or by trypsin leads to the degranulation of mast cells.
PAR-2 is a novel receptor that is involved in the activation of human mast cells.
PAR-2 agonist peptides, trypsin, and histamine are able to activate mast cells.
